title: Trump Tells Advisers He May Hold Off on Iran Strikes Absent New Provocations, Sources Say
dek: Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters Trump may refrain from attacking Iran without new provocations, while AP calls his path unresolved. Iran has warned of a “decisive response” to any renewed attack.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Topographic map of the Strait of Hormuz

keyPoints: Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that Trump told senior advisers he may hold off on attacking Iran if the U.S. faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Houthis.
Officials quoted by Reuters say Trump has not settled on a course; Meridian has not independently verified the sources’ accounts.
Iran’s deputy UN ambassador warned on Friday of an “immediate and decisive response” to any renewed U.S. or Israeli military attack, Anadolu reported.
Israeli media reported that Netanyahu discussed possible resumption of attacks on Iran with Eisenkot, who is forming the next government. Those reports are not independently verified.
The Kremlin said Putin, Xi and Trump will meet in Shenzhen on November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
body:
Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if the United States faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. The sources spoke on condition of anonymity, and Meridian has not independently verified their accounts.

Reuters reported that Trump has alternated between threats of new strikes and moves to wind down hostilities, and that officials say he has not settled on a course. In a separate report, the Associated Press described the administration’s path as unresolved, noting that Trump has backed away from additional strikes while also stepping back from the prospect of more talks with Iran’s negotiators.

## What the sources describe

According to the Reuters sources, Trump said in meetings with national security advisers and after intelligence briefings that he was considering holding off on strikes. Reuters also reported that he has expressed sympathy for regional allies who asked him not to return to full-scale war. In a broadcast interview with sports broadcaster Stephen A. Smith on Thursday, Trump said: “I could end it immediately, but at the request of the nations that I am looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a bit more civilly.”

Reuters reported that over the past two weeks Trump asked Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for their views. Both urged him not to resume attacks, according to a senior U.S. official and another person familiar with the matter, and Trump made no commitment either way. Two other people familiar with the discussion told Reuters that Trump told bin Salman on October 31 that he planned to attack after the midterm elections, and that the crown prince urged him to wait, arguing that economic sanctions were working.

## Official line and military posture

A White House official said in a statement, as quoted by Reuters: “As Commander-in-Chief, President Trump is the architect and sole decision-maker who holds all the cards and will always ensure that America’s interests are protected.” The statement added that “only President Trump knows what he will do, and when.”

Reuters reported that the U.S. military is ready to escalate if needed, and that a third aircraft carrier is moving into the Middle East in the coming days to replace one of the two now operating there, though all three could stay if needed. Two U.S. officials briefed on intelligence said the U.S. naval blockade and economic sanctions are hurting Iran’s economy and will keep up pressure on Tehran.

## Diplomacy and the Putin and Xi angle

Iran International, citing ABC News and senior U.S. officials, reported that Trump is expected to discuss Iran with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a trilateral meeting in China next week, with nuclear disarmament expected to be the main focus. The Kremlin has since confirmed the plan. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Saturday that Putin, Xi and Trump had agreed to a trilateral meeting on November 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, [Anadolu reported](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/kremlin-says-putin-xi-trump-to-hold-trilateral-meeting-in-shenzhen-on-nov-19/4125290), and [TASS carried](https://tass.com/politics/2218203) the same account. Anadolu also reported that Trump said on Nov. 8 he expected to meet Putin and Xi at the summit.

## Iran’s warning and the Israeli debate

Iran’s deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, Gholamhossein Darzi, told a Security Council meeting on Friday that the United States was waging an unlawful war of aggression against Tehran. He warned of an “immediate and decisive response” to any renewed American or Israeli military attack, [Anadolu Agency reported](https://www.anews.com.tr/middle-east/2026/11/14/iran-accuses-us-of-aggression-warns-of-decisive-response-to-renewed-attacks/amp). [TRT World](https://trtworld.com/article/4cad376aa720) carried the same warning.

Israeli media reports, cited by Anadolu, describe separate deliberations in Israel. Channel 12 reported that caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discussed the possible resumption of attacks on Iran with Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming the next government, at a meeting on Thursday, and sought to share Iran intelligence with him, [Anadolu reported](https://aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/netanyahu-discusses-possible-resumption-of-attacks-on-iran-with-eisenkot-israeli-media/4124854). Channel 12 said Eisenkot had not been aware that Mossad chief Roman Gofman was visiting Washington on the issue. Haaretz reported that Gofman met CIA Director John Ratcliffe. There was no comment from U.S. or Israeli authorities on the details of that visit.

Anadolu also cited KAN as reporting that Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir supports a military operation against Iran but does not believe the current timing is appropriate, and that the army sees no immediate Iranian threat requiring a new attack. Channel 12 had previously reported disagreements between Netanyahu and Zamir; Netanyahu’s office denied that report. Meridian has not independently verified these Israeli media accounts.

## What remains unclear

Both the Reuters and AP reports describe Trump’s position as unsettled. The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence did not respond to requests for comment, and the Saudi Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Reuters and AP both tie the question of renewed strikes to the wider conflict that Trump launched in February with Israel, which has become unpopular with U.S. voters.
